content.text: Skip to main content EASA - European Union Aviation Safety Agency Airlines and Aviation Köln, NRW 331,966 followers Safe air travel in Europe and worldwide See jobs Follow View all 1,049 employees Report this company About us The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) is at the centre of the European Union’s aviation safety system, ensuring that European citizens enjoy the highest common level of safety protection. It is an Agency of the European Union with specific regulatory responsibilities and executive tasks in the area of aviation safety. The Agency is based in Cologne, Germany, and has a satellite office in Brussels. In addition, the Agency has representative offices in Beijing, Montreal, Washington and Singapore, and is in the process of expanding its presence across different continents. The Agency has been operating for over 15 years, currently deploys around 800 professionals from across Europe and is open to recruit professionals from all Member States of the European Union, as well as from Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Switzerland. The Plan sets short-, mid- and long-term measures — including harmonised procedures, shared monitoring and data, updated guidance for crews and controllers, coordinated civil–military information exchange and collaboration with manufacturers to improve avionics resilience. “By working together…we have been able to create a strong plan that will enable the wider sector to come together to counter this threat.” — Florian Guillermet, EASA Executive Director This coordinated effort responds to growing RFI incidents and aligns with input from Member States and international partners to protect airspace capacity and keep operations safe and efficient.
